limitations: The adapter is transaction-neutral and relies on the active Frappe request/job/application transaction boundary.
No full pinned Frappe Bench site runtime failure-injection lab is implemented yet.
Static reachability is not runtime execution proof.

Frappe whitelist entrypoints are attributed from the Python decorated_definition AST node owned by the exact function; stacked and multiline @frappe.whitelist(...) decorator forms are supported and neighboring decorators never strengthen another function.
Aliased whitelist decorator names that require Python import/name resolution are not treated as proven @frappe.whitelist entrypoints in v0.1.

Frappe doc_events and scheduler_events are resolved only from one literal assignment with documented event keys and literal dotted handler strings/lists; scheduler cron maps are supported as literal nested maps.

Dynamic hook composition, later mutation/reassignment, duplicate literal keys, unknown event keys, and non-literal handler composition fail closed rather than producing optimistic hook dispatch edges.

Frappe enqueue resolution supports exact frappe.enqueue calls with a literal dotted positional or method= target, plus an unshadowed top-level function reference from the same Python module in positional or method= form.
Imported aliases, attribute references, dynamic or rebound enqueue targets, starred argument composition, and unrelated .enqueue methods do not produce optimistic Frappe dispatch edges.
frappe.enqueue_doc resolution supports exact calls with literal doctype and method identity; the document name may remain dynamic because it does not change the controller method target.
Dynamic enqueue_doc doctype/method identity, ambiguous conventional controllers, and custom or indirect controller resolution do not produce optimistic dispatch edges.

Document queue_action resolution supports AST-proven self.queue_action calls inside a conventional direct Document controller when the action is a literal identifier and the effective target method is defined by that controller.

External doc.queue_action receivers, dynamic action identity, starred argument composition, and framework-inherited inner actions without an app-local target fail closed; app-local _action methods take precedence exactly as Frappe queue_action does.
Document lifecycle dispatch is modeled only for conventional .../doctype/<name>/<name>.py controllers with exactly one explicit Document or frappe.model.document.Document subclass.

Indirect or aliased Document bases, multiple candidate controller classes, non-conventional controller paths, and storage primitives such as db_insert/db_update do not create optimistic lifecycle dispatch edges.
No Frappe production runtime corroboration profile is implemented in v0.1.

special_cases.semantics: Commits before TRUNCATE and cannot be represented as normal rollback-capable same-transaction atomicity.
Direct database mutation surfaces bypass normal Document events or validations and remain explicit audit boundaries.
